explanation: Lycophytes and Pteridophytes are two groups of seedless vascular plants. Lycophytes possess leaves called microphylls, which contain only a single strand of vascular tissue; this group includes club mosses, ground pines, spike mosses, and quillworts. Pteridophytes possess leaves called megaphylls, which contain several strands of vascular tissue; this group includes horsetails, whisk ferns, and true ferns.

opts: Microphylls are found on seed plants, while megaphylls are found on seedless plants.
Microphylls have only one strand of vascular tissue, whereas megaphylls have several strands.
Microphylls lack chlorophyll, whereas megaphylls contain it.
Microphylls are colonial structures, whereas megaphylls are multicellular.
